candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos I.46
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos I.46 (c. 350 AD)

'But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen' — Athanasius marks autō hē doxa nyn kai eis hēmeran aiōnos (to HIM be the glory now and unto the day of eternity) as a DOXOLOGICAL-WORSHIP-OF-CHRIST anchor that the Arians cannot consistently maintain. The doxa-directed-to-Christ is the creature's-worship-act that is owed to God-by-nature alone (the first-commandment exclusion of creature-worship). If Christ were a creature-by-nature, this doxology would be idolatrous; the verse's own-internal-logic-positively-requires Christ's-divine-essence. Pairs with 2 Pet 3:18 with Rev 1:6 (autō hē doxa kai to kratos eis tous aiōnas) and Rev 5:13 (autō hē doxa kai hē timē) as the canonical worship-directed-to-Christ Apocalyptic-Petrine triplet.

candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / De Incarnatione Verbi §6
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §6 (c. 350 AD)

'The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance' — Athanasius marks mē boulomenos tinas apolesthai alla pantas eis metanoian chōrēsai (not willing any to perish but all to come to-repentance) as the DIVINE-UNIVERSAL-SALVIFIC-WILL Petrine-anchor. The divine-patience (makrothymia) is itself-incarnational: the Word's-incarnation IS the divine-patience-extended-in-time, giving humanity-time to repent. Athanasius's DI §6-7 anti-Manichaean reading of evil-as-privation-of-good rests on this universal-salvific-will: God-cannot-be-the-author-of-evil because his-will-is-toward-universal-restoration.
